questionText:
The number of units of a product sold in three different years and the respective net profits are presented in the figure above. The cost/unit in Year 3 was ₹ 1, which was half the cost/unit in Year 2. The cost/unit in Year 3 was one-third of the cost/unit in Year 1. Taxes were paid on the selling price at 10%, 13% and 15% respectively for the three years. Net profit is calculated as the difference between the selling price and the sum of cost and taxes paid in that year.

The ratio of the selling price in Year 2 to the selling price in Year 3 is ________.
explanation:
Given Data from the Graph and Question:
- Year 2: Number of units sold = $200$, Net profit = ₹ $296$, Tax rate = $13\%$
- Year 3: Number of units sold = $300$, Net profit = ₹ $210$, Tax rate = $15\%$
- Cost per unit in Year 3 = ₹ $1$
- Cost per unit in Year 2 = $2 \times 1 = \text{₹ } 2$

Year 2 Total Selling Price ($SP_2$):
Total Cost ($TC_2$) = $200 \times 2 = \text{₹ } 400$
Net Profit = $SP_2 - (TC_2 + \text{Tax}_2)$
$296 = SP_2 - (400 + 0.13 \times SP_2)$
$296 = 0.87 \times SP_2 - 400$
$0.87 \times SP_2 = 696 \implies SP_2 = \frac{696}{0.87} = 800$

Year 3 Total Selling Price ($SP_3$):
Total Cost ($TC_3$) = $300 \times 1 = \text{₹ } 300$
Net Profit = $SP_3 - (TC_3 + \text{Tax}_3)$
$210 = SP_3 - (300 + 0.15 \times SP_3)$
$210 = 0.85 \times SP_3 - 300$
$0.85 \times SP_3 = 510 \implies SP_3 = \frac{510}{0.85} = 600$

Ratio of Selling Price (Year 2 to Year 3):
$\frac{SP_2}{SP_3} = \frac{800}{600} = \frac{4}{3} = 4:3$

Hence, option (A) is the correct answer.
